summary: The root QBR refers to a type of small bird, specifically a lark. It is known by several similar-sounding names, such as qubbar, qubbarah, and qunbura. The plural form is qanabir.
lane: قُبَّرٌ ذ (S, Msb, K) and (K) and (S, K) and , this last occurring in a Rejez, to be cited below, (S,) The [ lark; ] a kind of bird, (S, K,) resembling the حُمَّرَة ; (TA;) a kind of small bird; (Msb:) n. un. قُبَّرَةٌ (S, Msb, K) and قُبَرَةٌ (K) and قُنْبُرَةٌ , (S, Msb,) which last is the form used by the vulgar, (S,) or it is not allowable, or it is a form of weak authority, (K,) and is also pronounced قُنْبَرَةٌ : (Msb:) pl. of قنبراء , (S, K,) and of قنبرة , (Msb,) قَنَابِرُ . (S, Msb, K.) AO cites, from a Rejez of Jendel Ibn-El-Muthennà Et- Tahawee, جَآءَ الشِّتَآءُ وَٱجْثَأَلَّ القُنْبُرُ [ The winter came, and the lark plumed himself ]. (S.)

headwords.def: قَبَرَ, aor. قَبُرَ and قَبِرَ, inf. n. قَبْرٌ (S, Msb, K) and مَقْبَرٌ, (K,) He buried a corpse; (S, Msb, K:) concealed it in the earth. (TA.)

اقبرهُ He made him to be buried: so in the Kur, lxxx. 21: (Fr, S:) where it is meant that man is not made by God to be thrown, when dead, to the dogs, (S,) or to the birds and wild beasts. (Fr.) He ordered that he should be buried. (S, Mgh, Msb.) [ He permitted that he should be buried. ] The tribe of Temeem said to El-Hejjáj, who had slain Sálih the son of 'Abder-Rahmán, أَقْبِرْنَا صَالِحًا, meaning, Permit us to bury Sálih.
قَبْرٌ A grave, tomb, sepulchre, or place of burial, of a human being: (K:) pl. قُبُور. (S, Msb, K.)

قُبَّرٌ (S, Msb, K) and (K) and (S, K) and, this last occurring in a Rejez, to be cited below, (S,) The [ lark; ] a kind of bird, (S, K,) resembling the حُمَّرَة; (TA;) a kind of small bird; (Msb:) n. un. قُبَّرَةٌ (S, Msb, K) and قُبَرَةٌ (K) and قُنْبُرَةٌ, (S, Msb,) which last is the form used by the vulgar, (S,) or it is not allowable, or it is a form of weak authority, (K,) and is also pronounced قُنْبَرَةٌ: (Msb:) pl. of قنبراء, (S, K,) and of قنبرة, (Msb,) قَنَابِرُ.

مَقْبُرَةٌ and مَقْبَرَةٌ (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and مَقْبِرَةٌ and مِقْبَرَةٌ (K) and, (Lth, S, Mgh,) with fet-h only, (Mgh,) this last occurring in poetry, (S,) but agreeable with analogy, (IB,) and. (MF, and TA voce أَلُوكٌ, [under which see some remarks on words of this form in the present work,]) A cemetery, burial-place, or place of graves: (Msb, K:) or the place of a grave: (Mgh:) or the last of the above words has this latter signification: (Lth:) pl. (of مقبرة and مقبر, Mgh) مَقَابِرُ.
مَقْبَرِىٌّ and مَقْبُرِىٌّ applied to a man [ A keeper of a cemetery: or of a grave or tomb: or a gravedigger ]. (S.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
